definition: Deliberate sampling is an intentional plan for choosing research participants rather than relying on who is easiest to include. In this context, it is used to make sure marginalized and underserved groups are adequately represented so their experiences can be examined.

reasons: The packet only states that “deliberate sampling plans are needed to examine those most marginalized and underserved,” but it does not define deliberate sampling as an “intentional plan for choosing research participants rather than relying on who is easiest to include.”

The packet supports the general idea of ensuring marginalized/underserved groups are examined, but it does not explicitly support the full rationale in the definition (“so their experiences can be examined”) in the way the definition phrases it.

The packet supports that deliberate sampling plans are needed to examine marginalized and underserved groups, but it does not explicitly support the broader definition that this is an intentional plan for choosing participants instead of convenience-based recruitment.

The claim that the purpose is to ensure marginalized and underserved groups are adequately represented is stronger than the source, which only says such groups need to be examined; it does not state a representativeness requirement.
